concept.shortExplanation: Attention and feed-forward blocks are not the only reason transformers work — the plumbing around them is doing real load-bearing work. A residual connection adds each block's input back to its output, so the block only has to learn a correction and gradients get an unobstructed path back to earlier layers. Layer normalisation rescales each token's activations to a consistent statistic, which stops the values drifting as depth accumulates. Remove either one and deep stacks stop training. The activation traces here are real hidden states pulled from every layer of a live model.
concept.ahaMoment: Depth was never blocked by a lack of ideas about what layers should compute. It was blocked by numbers drifting and gradients dying, and two pieces of plumbing fixed both.
